claims.statement: Antiplatelet/anticoagulant utilization and VTE/bleeding burden varied across three parent trials and mixed clinical indications. Class Ns and endpoints overlap; no verified deduplicated combined-user count or randomized prophylaxis effect follows from pooled descriptive rates.

Adjusted anticoagulant landmark VTE odds were lower, but the source gives OR.45CI.26-.77P.004 in abstract/text and.39CI.22-.69P.001 inTable5, unresolved. Neither estimate establishes causal prevention efficacy, an absolute risk reduction or a specificDOACdose benefit.

Adjusted baseline antiplatelet use had a nominal positiveIHDassociationOR1.86CI1.09-3.14P.022, while otherbaseline/landmarkCIs included1. The abstract blanket-nullstatement is incomplete; no causal aspirin harm or equal bleeding safety is established.

All adjusted OS/PFS comparisons were nonsignificant, including anticoagulantbaselineOSHR1.27CI1.00-1.61P.051. SelectedlandmarkNs1568/1348 and observational exposure preclude equivalence/noeffect or aspirin anticancer-benefit conclusions.

sourceQualifications.description: Parent trials randomized myeloma regimens, not antithrombotics. This posthoc antithrombotic analysis is observational, with confounding by indication/comorbidity and treatment of existing events. Covariate adjustment does not prove causation, absolute prevention benefit, aspirin harm or an anticancer effect.

MAIA737/POLLUX569/CASTOR498=1804 is a pooled report of existing three trial families. MAIA newlydiagnosed/transplantineligible differsfromrelapsed/refractoryPOLLUX/CASTOR. CASTORbortezomib/dexamethasone is not IMiD-containing despite broad abstract wording. No new independent trials or people added by this report.
